Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd."
Document: "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instrument Ltd."

The difference: "Instruments" vs "Instrument" — plural vs singular. This is spelling drift / morphological variance of the same company name. Same entity. Best value: which one? The register is the canonical record; the rules say spelling drift = same-entity. For same-entity, what's the best value? The rules specify best_value for different-entity = document's; for document-noise = register's. For same-entity, presumably use the register's canonical form (like the number/year rule says register's canonical form). The register here is "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd." — actually the actual legal name of the company is "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd." I believe. But per rules, register canonical form is safe for same-entity.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd." (register's canonical form), why: singular vs plural "Instrument(s)" is minor spelling drift of the same company.
